nodes.label: ClientFlow Design System
nodes.rationale: Source of truth for shared product UI (interface-design scope: dashboards, client screens, settings). Direction is a calm, focused workbench for freelancers and small service businesses: legible, dense-but-clean, with a single indigo accent - explicitly not a glass/blue SaaS dashboard and not a marketing site. Marketing-only patterns live in a separate marketing.md file.

nodes.label: Indigo Accent
nodes.rationale: Slate neutrals with one indigo accent (#4f46e5) chosen so the product reads quiet, airy, and predictable and does not resemble a generic glass/blue SaaS dashboard. Semantic status colors (emerald for success, red for destructive/errors) are used sparingly.

nodes.label: Data View States
nodes.rationale: Every data view must have a loading state (role=status), a retryable error state (role=alert), an empty state, and a no-results state so all states are accessible and predictable.

nodes.label: Responsive Tables
nodes.rationale: Desktop client list renders as a table hidden below md; mobile renders stacked cards. Both are rendered so only one is in the accessibility tree at a time.

nodes.label: Workspace-Scoped Authorization
nodes.rationale: Every protected route authenticates the Bearer token and requires the X-Workspace-Id header; data access is scoped to workspace membership so one user can never read or mutate another workspace's clients. The API remains the real security boundary; client-side route guards are only UX.

nodes.label: Session Persistence
nodes.rationale: Access token and active workspace ID are kept in sessionStorage for the current tab only; no client data is stored in browser storage. A session provider restores the token on reload and revalidates it against GET /auth/me.

nodes.label: JWT Access Token
nodes.rationale: Short-lived HS256 access tokens only; no refresh tokens or server-side revocation yet, so logout means removing the token client-side. Claims include sub, iss, aud, iat, exp, jti, tokenType=access and carry no email/workspace/role data. Rate limiting, account lockout, email verification, password reset, and MFA are intentionally deferred.

nodes.label: Client Management
nodes.rationale: Any current workspace member can manage clients; granular role permissions are intentionally not part of the MVP. Cross-workspace lookups return the same CLIENT_NOT_FOUND so the API never reveals whether another workspace owns an ID. Client data is never logged.

nodes.label: QUERY /clients/search
nodes.rationale: QUERY is a read-only, idempotent alternative for structured filters (hasEmail, hasPhone); it does not replace GET /clients. POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE never invoke the structured search handler.
